post_text:
Kubernetes kills your Java process before the JVM even knows it's in trouble.

You aren't just managing heap; you're managing the container's patience. 🛡️

Most OOMKills happen because engineers treat -Xmx as the only memory limit that matters.

Set MaxRAMPercentage to 75% to leave breathing room for Metaspace, Code Cache, and thread stacks.

Monitor container_memory_working_set_bytes instead of JVM heap metrics to see what the kernel actually sees.

Match InitialRAMPercentage to your max to prevent the OS from reclaiming memory during a sudden heap expansion. 🚀
lesson_extracted: Prevent OOMKills by accounting for non-heap overhead and monitoring container-level metrics instead of just JVM internals.
